record.paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
record.original_question: Assume the P-ideal dichotomy, namely that for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of some set S, either there is an uncountable set T ⊆ S such that every countable subset of T belongs to I, or S can be decomposed into countably many pieces with no infinite subset in I. Under this assumption, are the following equivalent: (1) every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system; and (2) b = ℵ_2, where b is the minimum cardinality of an unbounded family in N^N under eventual domination?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A family $\mathcal I$ of countable subsets of a set $S$ is called a P-ideal if $\mathcal I$ is closed under finite unions, hereditary (closed under taking subsets), and $\sigma$-directed modulo finite (for every sequence $\{A_n\}_{n\in\omega}\subseteq\mathcal I$ there exists $A\in\mathcal I$ with $A_n\setminus A$ finite for every $n$). The P-ideal Dichotomy (PID) is the assertion that for every set $S$ and every P-ideal $\mathcal I$ of countable subsets of $S$, at least one of the following holds:
(a) there exists an uncountable $T\subseteq S$ such that every countable subset of $T$ belongs to $\mathcal I$;
(b) $S$ can be written as a countable union $S=\bigcup_{n\in\omega} S_n$ such that no $S_n$ contains an infinite subset belonging to $\mathcal I$.

Let $\mathfrak{b}$ denote the bounding number, i.e. the least cardinality of a family $\mathcal F\subseteq \mathbb N^{\mathbb N}$ that is unbounded under eventual domination $\le^*$ (where $f\le^* g$ means $f(n)\le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$).

A biorthogonal system in a Banach space $X$ is a family $\{(x_\alpha,x_\alpha^*)\}_{\alpha\in\Gamma}\subseteq X\times X^*$ such that $x_\alpha^*(x_\beta)=\delta_{\alpha\beta}$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\Gamma$.

Problem. Assume PID. Are the following two statements equivalent?
(1) Every non-separable Banach space admits an uncountable biorthogonal system.
(2) $\mathfrak{b}=\aleph_2$.
artifact.status_search_result: Brech and Todorcevic established under PID that the equivalence with $\mathfrak{b}=\aleph_2$ holds when "non-separable Banach space" is restricted to non-separable Asplund spaces; more generally, under PID, every non-separable Banach space of density strictly smaller than $\mathfrak{b}$ with weak*-sequentially compact dual ball admits an uncountable biorthogonal system. The full equivalence for arbitrary non-separable Banach spaces does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Biorthogonality in Banach spaces and the P-ideal dichotomy (Brech–Todorcevic)
status_evidence.snippet: Assuming the P-ideal dichotomy, the following are equivalent to b=ω2: every nonseparable Asplund space has an uncountable biorthogonal system; every nonseparable Asplund space has a nonseparable quotient with monotone Schauder basis.
status_evidence.claim: PID-equivalence with b=aleph_2 has been proved for non-separable Asplund spaces, a strict subclass of all non-separable Banach spaces.
